english_verification.review_scope: Read Y58 opening history and representative English flavor text on the Lapnam slums, markets, gangs, and mercenary recruitment. Read the country Wiki stub and the arena chunk for related background only. This is not an exhaustive mission or event audit. The primary compared native idea names/descriptions with current English localisation keys (formatting codes stripped); original sources and optional sets are kept separate. Wide source bounds are locator envelopes, not exhaustive line-by-line audits. No formal validators, tests, builds or browser checks were run.
unresolved: The country Wiki page is explicitly a stub and contains only brief identity information; arena history is drawn from the related Teplinbasiet Arena page, not treated as a full national history.
The exact mission-tree rework date and full route reachability were not established.
A mission objective to unite Bomdan does not by itself establish a Tag change; no such change is asserted here.

rationale.colonization: Colonization is not the mission tree's main form of expansion.
rationale.complexity: Mercenaries, nobles, subjects, and ruler culture and religion requirements interact.
rationale.dark_story: Military nobles and expansion create grey areas, but ordinary warfare alone is not evidence of atrocities.
rationale.difficulty: Endgame conditions are strict; no campaign was playtested.
rationale.diplomacy: Subjects, neighbouring-country interactions, and a union objective matter.
rationale.early_pressure: Nearby rivals, allies, and resources complicate the opening, but it is not a hopeless start.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Magic and artifice are not defining themes of the country.
rationale.narrative_density: The arena, mercenary nobility, urban slums, and northern contest form a connected story.
rationale.tall_play: Capital security and market construction matter, but are not the main axis of play.
rationale.trade_economy: Mercenary upkeep and the arms market make financial management important.
rationale.warfare: Unifying Bomdan and challenging the Command both rely on warfare.

identity.appearance: An established mercenary-arena kingdom in 1444, ruled by Metnikhren.
identity.formation_scope: Y58 can pursue a Bomdan Empire internally and a conditional Fourth Command route; a Tag change is not established as necessary.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Accepting new ideas on formation depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text: Centred around the Dekkhang feudal contract, the mercenary nobility of Lot Dekkhang enjoy privileges not seen in other kingdoms, such as reduced taxes and levies. These mercenary nobles, called Daulophs, traditionally use these excess men and gold for investments into mercenary companies. For us, we benefit from having a larger mass of ready mercenaries, as well as capable men to lead them.

description.text: Located on the highest hill of the city, the Teplinbasiet stands tallest amongst our city. One of the High Temples sought after by Harimar, the tigerfolk would conquer Lapnam Amrik, repressing and subjugating the populace under a zealous religious governor. Now under human jurisdiction, the temple has been subverted, with its conversion to a theatre and arena - the former teaching old folktales, and the latter showcasing combat prowess.

description.text: Composed of many languages, Mercenary Dialect was developed with the purpose of exchanging information with many foreign clientele. Even past their time as mercenaries, the Daulophs of Lot Dekkhang commonly use it to communicate with foreign dignitaries - or to bewilder them.

description.text: In the early 16th century, the Great Weapon Market at Lapnam Amrik had bloated to a massive size. Miles of stalls, violence between competing bands, and corrupt clerks undermined trade and the law. In 1546, Dimche Beokhting was appointed as manager of the market. She reorganised the stalls, settled disputes, hired diligent clerks, and created a new form of Bookkeeping named after her. The result was an efficient market, free of violence, and much more open for foreign trade than in centuries past.

description.text: Established in 1597 by the famous veteran Tirakseb of the Grand Contingent, one of the most notorious High Philosophy academies in the world began following a disastrous defeat of the Grand Contingent. Originally military oriented, it expanded to host a wide variety of subjects, from Philosophy to Dekkhangi Literature. Now, there is a large surplus of scholars and academics whose ideas we can apply to the state.

description.text: In the last few centuries, cannons have become a common form of warfare in Haless. But the defensive infrastructure present in Bomdan needed special attention in order to be overcome. To this end, the development of the Sphangaokbrach "Copper Ram'' Batteries in 1680 gave Dekkhangi generals the ability to overcome the many forts found throughout Bomdan.

description.text: Historically, the steel-bind contract, otherwise known as the Dekkhang, was a loose set of disjointed laws and firm privileges afforded to the Daulophs. This had always caused local officials to struggle with all the contradictory or vague laws that arose in the centuries after its establishment. Between 1732 and 1734, Metnikhren IV created a royal constitution, codifying the Dekkhang and adding new laws for the modern era, centralising the kingdom in the process.

player_overview.avoid_if: Players who dislike dependence on mercenaries and subjects, or want an endgame goal without ruler-culture and religion requirements.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Use mercenaries and subjects to gain leverage early, unite Bomdan and reform the capital in midgame, then contest northern hegemony according to your chosen route.
player_overview.overview: Lot Dekkhang is Bomdan's mercenary kingdom, ruled in 1444 by Metnikhren. Use arena nobles, mercenary companies, and subjects to bring neighbouring peoples together while addressing the capital's slums and ethnic tensions. Later, a Swallow Hobgoblin ruler who meets the religious and mercenary requirements can contest the Command's imperial throne; this is a conditional route, not a free annexation.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy mercenary economics, military-political classes, and expansion along several fronts.
signature_features: Arena nobles and mercenaries sit at the center of the country's politics.
Subject administration and multi-ethnic manpower connect the campaign to Bomdan's unification.
The Swallow Hobgoblin route can grant a Restoration of Union casus belli against the Command.
player_overview.tagline: Turn a mercenary-noble arena into a state machine, and take a Bomdan kingdom to the threshold of the Command.

reasons: Mercenary-noble politics and the arena give the country a strong identity.
Multi-ethnic manpower and subject administration add layers to expansion.
The conditional Command route provides a major endgame objective.
warnings: The late-game union route does not guarantee success.
Managing mercenaries and subjects requires attention.

positive_indicators: Reforming the capital's slums and protecting commerce.
Integrating hobgoblin refugees and multi-ethnic manpower.
values.rationale: Slum reform, market security, and multi-ethnic forces are concrete public benefits. The missions also center military nobles, subject rule, and a conditional bid for hegemony. Ordinary conquest and monarchy are not penalized directly. Treatment of residents across the full route is unverified, so the assessment remains neutral.
red_flags: Some conquest narratives use language of civilizational superiority.
Military nobles may receive political priority.
